answers.reason: A junior professor does not hold a central leadership office or senior rank required for the university-wide senate.
University-wide budget allocation is reserved for central leadership and faculty deans rather than fixed-term junior professors.
As a professor, the junior professor holds sufficient academic rank to participate in faculty-level appointment committees.
Holding a professorship within the faculty entitles the junior professor to participate in the faculty council.
As a professor who teaches in the faculty, the junior professor has the rank to take part in faculty teaching committees.
Professorial rank and teaching duties qualify the junior professor to sit on the faculty's examination board.
Leading a research group as a professor qualifies the junior professor to take part in the faculty's internal research funding round.
As a teaching professor, the junior professor outranks or matches the level required for a working group revising degree modules.
A junior professor who teaches and leads a research group has the rank to participate in procuring teaching laboratory equipment.
Because those with higher rank may take part in bodies below their level, a junior professor is permitted to join this lower-level planning round.
